title: Dynamic types, coercion, and equality
intro: JavaScript discovers types at run time, coerces values between types in operators and conditionals, and offers three equality algorithms. This module teaches the seven primitives, why typeof lies about null, how + picks concat vs add, when to use === vs == vs Object.is, and how JSON serialization differs from real JavaScript values.

conceptCards.title: Primitives copy; objects alias
conceptCards.summary: Seven primitives assign by value. Objects, arrays, and functions assign by reference.
conceptCards.example: `const b = a` on an object — mutations are shared.

conceptCards.title: typeof null is 'object'
conceptCards.summary: Historical engine bug. Always test `value === null` separately before treating a value as an object.

conceptCards.title: + picks string or number
conceptCards.summary: If either operand is a string, + concatenates. Otherwise ToNumber and add. Objects use ToPrimitive first.

conceptCards.title: Three equality algorithms
conceptCards.summary: `===` strict, no coercion. `==` coerces types. `Object.is` / SameValueZero handle NaN and ±0 differently.

conceptCards.title: BigInt past 2⁵³
conceptCards.summary: number loses precision above MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. Use bigint with n suffix for snowflake IDs.

conceptCards.title: Eight falsy values
conceptCards.summary: false, 0, -0, 0n, '', null, undefined, NaN. Everything else is truthy — including [] and {}.

conceptCards.title: TypeScript erases at run time
conceptCards.summary: TS checks types at compile time only. Run time is plain JS — validate JSON.parse at boundaries.
conceptCards.example: Zod or manual typeof guards on API input

conceptCards.title: JSON is not JavaScript
conceptCards.summary: stringify drops undefined and functions. parse returns plain objects. Never eval. Guard __proto__.
